verifiedInvariants: The current physical model uses orders for both an open client exchange request and the later active/completed service order lifecycle.

Open request state is represented on orders by statuses such as new/waiting_responses plus exchange_status, exchange_round, exchange deadline and response limits; master_exchange_responses are keyed to the same orders.id as request_id.

After professional acceptance, the same order_id is enriched by diagnostics, checklist/media, parts reservations, quality checks, handover, warranty and dispatch state rather than being materialized as a separate RepairOrder row.
Repair execution is stage-gated; accepting an order can transition workflow from intake to diagnostics and updates orders.status to process.
Order visibility/write scope is resolved from the authoritative Identity context with staged legacy fallback: client by ownership, master by master_id, STO by sto_id.
Service scheduling and dispatch write order date/time/master/resource planning state, creating explicit cross-domain coupling with Master, Booking and Organization.
domainDebt: Target semantic invariant ServiceRequest != RepairOrder is not physically represented today: the same orders aggregate spans request/exchange and repair lifecycle.
Because request and repair share orders.id, ownership boundaries for scheduling, dispatch and exchange acceptance are coupled and must be separated by contracts before any physical split.
Do not rename orders to RepairOrder or declare ServiceRequest separately VERIFIED until a migration/compatibility plan exists.

verifiedInvariants: organizations is the physical organization store and supports service_station and parts_store organizations migrated from legacy STO and seller profiles.
organization_members stores business membership semantics including member role, position, branch unit, status and organization-local permissions.
